This integration connects your **homee** box (Z-Wave, Zigbee, EnOcean,
depending on its cubes) to Gladys Assistant, locally: the devices paired with
the box become Gladys devices, their states follow the box live and Gladys
controls them through it.

> Unofficial integration, not affiliated with homee GmbH. It has **never been
> tested with a real homee**: it was written from the pyHomee library and the
> homee integration of Home Assistant, and tested against a simulated box.
> Your feedback is welcome.

## What is supported

- **Lights**: on/off, brightness, colour temperature.
- **Plain wall switches** (the "on/off switch" profiles, double, with input,
  Wi-Fi): on/off, dimmer.
- **Plugs, metering relays and any other device**: state, power, energy
  (cumulative index), and "Turn on" / "Turn off" buttons behind an option
  (see below).
- **Roller shutters**: open, close, stop, position.
- **Thermostats and radiator heads**: temperature, setpoint, valve opening,
  battery, heating mode (read).
- **Hot water**: temperature, setpoint (capped).
- **Sensors**: opening, window, motion, presence, leak and flood, smoke,
  carbon monoxide, tamper, low battery, temperature, humidity, illuminance,
  CO2, UV, wind, rain, current, voltage.
- **Locks, garage doors, gates, impulse relays, water valves, sirens, the
  homee mode**: read-only state, and buttons (or a list for the mode) that
  work only when you allow them. In v1, the Open / Close / Stop buttons exist
  for motorised garage doors and entrance gates only; other doors and window
  motors show their state, their impulse buttons stay.
- Remotes and wall buttons (presses), homeegrams and the INOVA alarm (always
  read-only) are not handled yet.

## Configuration

1. In the homee app, preferably create a **user of its own** for Gladys.
2. Note the **local IP address** of the box (Settings → homee, or your
   router). Give it a fixed address.
3. In Gladys, Integrations → homee: type the IP address, the user name and the
   password, then **Test the connection**.
4. In the **Discovery** tab, add the devices you want.

The password is a secret field: it is kept by Gladys in its database, never
shown again, and sent only to your homee (as its SHA-512 fingerprint, like the
homee apps do). The integration only uses the local connection of the box
(port 7681), never my.hom.ee.

## Safety: what stays read-only

A "turn everything off" (Google Home, Alexa, HomeKit, MCP, a scene) must never
reach a valve, a lock, a siren, a heating or an unknown load. Only lights and
plain wall switches therefore get a switch in Gladys; every other device has
a read-only state and buttons, refused while the matching option is off (all
are off by default):

| Option                        | What it allows                                                         |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Allow plug control            | Turn on / Turn off buttons of plugs, metering relays and other devices |
| Allow heating control         | Thermostat and hot water setpoints, on/off of electric heaters         |
| Allow lock control            | Lock, Unlock, Unlatch                                                  |
| Allow door and gate control   | Open, Close, Stop (garage doors, entrance gates), impulses             |
| Allow valve control           | Open / Close water valves                                              |
| Allow siren control           | Sound / Stop the siren                                                 |
| Allow changing the homee mode | Home, Sleeping, Away, Vacation (a list)                                |

For each of these commands, the integration reads the state of the device just
before, refuses when that state is unknown or moving (a door whose target
differs from its position is moving), checks the option one last time just
before sending, and waits for the box to confirm. Without a confirmation in
time, Gladys shows "Command sent, without confirmation from the homee": check
the device.

The **protective** commands — lock, close the valve, stop a door, turn off,
stop the siren — are never refused because of the state of the device and
are always sent (a leak while a valve opens must be able to close it). No
command waits behind the confirmation of another. A lock, a door or a valve
that does not report the state asked for in time (30 s, 90 s, 60 s) shows
"State not confirmed" on its badge, until it reports a state. Two presses of
an impulse button less than 2 s apart count as one. A door whose direction
(reversed or not in homee) is unknown or changed since it was added refuses
Open / Close. A command that cannot leave within 3.5 s is refused, never sent
late.

The hot water setpoint is capped at **55 °C** by default (scalding risk),
adjustable up to **60 °C** at most, the setpoint of a warm water circuit
included. Any setpoint outside the range shown in Gladys is refused. The
valves of radiator heads are never controlled directly: they follow their
setpoint. On an on/off water valve, the meaning of "on" (open or closed) is
still to be checked on a real box: the buttons are therefore named "Turn on"
/ "Turn off".

## Energy

The cumulative energy of a plug or a meter is an index Gladys bills: every
rise is counted in full. The integration guards it like the P1 Monitor
integration does:

- never 0; a drop or an implausible jump (more than 25 kW on average since
  the last reading) is **held**: the last accepted value is sent again, the
  badge of the device shows the kWh waiting, and the log says so; the hold is
  kept in `/data`, even across a restart;
- it is never confirmed by repetition nor by time: only the **"Accept the
  held index"** action of the configuration takes it, **in two clicks**. The
  first click takes nothing: it lists every index held on the device chosen
  (feature, drop or jump, from → to, kWh). A second click within 60 s takes
  exactly that list — each value shown, plus what the device may draw until
  its next reading — and answers with the kWh counted; if the list changed
  meanwhile, it is listed again. The badge of the device sums up all its
  holds (how many, the kWh at stake). Saving the configuration or a
  reconnection never accepts anything;
- a device added again starts from a fresh guard;
- the **total** of an energy meter (which may also count the plugs of the
  box) is a plain value, never an index: the energy of the plugs is not
  counted twice.

## Connection and errors

- A token is asked from the box when connecting and kept in memory only; it is
  renewed before its end, never in a loop. When the box refuses the live
  connection while its port answers, a new token is asked at the next try; a
  network failure keeps the token.
- A lost live connection is opened again after 5 s, then 10 s, 20 s… up to
  5 minutes between two tries. The whole box is read again every 10 minutes;
  without an answer within 30 s, the connection is opened again.
- **Refused credentials**: the integration stops and notes it in `/data`
  (without the user name or the password, only a salted fingerprint). Next
  automatic try after 1 h, then 2 h, 4 h… up to 24 h; "Test the connection"
  or saving the configuration tries at once (the same credentials refused
  again wait longer).
- If the box asks to slow down (HTTP 429), the integration pauses (1 minute to
  6 hours), kept even across a restart.
- "Test the connection" reuses the connection in use when there is one.

## Known limits

- Never tested with a real homee (see above): the profiles and the meaning of
  some values come from pyHomee and Home Assistant.
- Feature names are set when the device is added.
- Remote presses, homeegrams, groups and the INOVA alarm are not handled yet.

## Konfigurationseinstellungen

Diese Einstellungen fragt homee in seinem Konfigurationsbildschirm in Gladys ab.

| Einstellung | Typ | Pflichtfeld | Beschreibung |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your homee devices in Gladys | `section` | Nein | The devices paired with your homee box (Z-Wave, Zigbee, EnOcean) are offered in the Discovery tab: lights, switches, plugs, shutters, thermostats, contact, motion, leak, smoke sensors, temperature, humidity, consumption. The states follow the box live, through its local connection only. Plugs, heating, locks, doors and gates, valves, sirens and the homee mode stay read-only until you allow them below, and they are never switches. Never tested with a real box yet. Unofficial, not affiliated with homee. |
| Address of the homee | `string` | Ja | The local IP address of your homee box, like 192.168.1.60 (shown in the homee app, Settings → homee). Local only: not my.hom.ee. |
| homee user name | `string` | Ja | A user of the homee box, the one you log in with in the homee app. A user of its own for Gladys is best. |
| Password | `secret` | Ja | The password of this homee user. Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, and sent only to your homee. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | Nein | Used for the names of the features of the devices added from now on. |
| Minimum interval between two readings of a sensor (s) | `number` | Nein | Some devices report every second (power meters): Gladys keeps the last reading at this pace. Switches, lights, contact and motion sensors are never delayed. |
| Allow plug control from Gladys | `boolean` | Nein | Off by default: the load behind a plug, a metering relay or any device that is not a light nor a plain wall switch is unknown (a heater, a freezer…), so it is never a switch: its state is read-only and it has "Turn on" and "Turn off" buttons, which work only when this option is on. |
| Allow heating control from Gladys | `boolean` | Nein | Off by default: setpoints of thermostats and hot water, and the on/off buttons of electric heaters, are read-only. On, Gladys can change them, from the dashboard and scenes. |
| Highest hot water setpoint (°C) | `number` | Nein | A hot water setpoint above it is refused (scalding risk): 55 °C by default, 60 °C at most. |
| Allow lock control from Gladys | `boolean` | Nein | Off by default: locks are read-only. On, their "Lock", "Unlock" and "Unlatch" buttons work, from the dashboard and scenes. |
| Allow door and gate control from Gladys | `boolean` | Nein | Off by default: garage doors, gates, doors, window motors and impulse relays are read-only. On, their "Open", "Close", "Stop" and impulse buttons work. |
| Allow valve control from Gladys | `boolean` | Nein | Off by default: water valves are read-only. On, their open and close buttons work. Radiator valves always follow their thermostat. |
| Allow siren control from Gladys | `boolean` | Nein | Off by default: sirens are read-only. On, their "Sound the siren" and "Stop the siren" buttons work. |
| Allow changing the homee mode from Gladys | `boolean` | Nein | Off by default: the mode of the box (home, sleeping, away, vacation), which your homeegrams may use to arm an alarm, is read-only. On, it can be chosen from a list. The INOVA alarm is always read-only. |

## So installierst du homee in Gladys

1. Öffne in Gladys **Integrationen**: homee erscheint im Katalog neben den nativen Integrationen, mit einem Community-Badge.
2. Klicke auf **Installieren**. Gladys lädt das Docker-Image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-homee:0.1.1`) herunter, startet es in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox und erzeugt die Oberfläche der Integration (Geräte, Erkennung und Konfiguration).
3. Öffne den Bildschirm **Konfiguration** der Integration, fülle die Einstellungen aus und speichere.
4. Du kannst sie auch direkt über die URL ihres Repositorys installieren: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-homee](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-homee).

homee benötigt Gladys `>=5.1.0`. Der Katalog in Gladys wird stündlich aktualisiert, eine neue Version ist also spätestens eine Stunde nach ihrer Veröffentlichung verfügbar.

Du nutzt Gladys noch nicht? Es ist kostenlos und Open Source: [folge der Installationsanleitung](/de/docs/), um loszulegen.

## Über externe Integrationen

homee ist eine **externe Integration**: eine Community-Integration, die als Docker-Container verpackt und auf GitHub veröffentlicht wird. Gladys installiert sie mit einem Klick und führt sie in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox aus. Sie wird von [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7) veröffentlicht und gepflegt, nicht vom Gladys-Kernteam.

- [Alle Integrationen durchsuchen](/de/docs/integrations/), native und aus der Community
